_comment: Which sections of Smyth's Greek Grammar (1920) the word box quotes for each grammatical category of a tagged parse. The categories are those of the 9-position AGDT tag that GLAUx uses (tools/greek.py decode_postag). The text shown is always Smyth's own; this file only records which section was chosen and why. Chosen for the Workshop in November 2026; change any line and rebuild. Categories with no entry (singular, masculine, 3rd person ...) get no note.

adjective: Smyth's opening statement on the syntax of adjectives
adverb: the opening of Smyth's section on adverbs, with the two kinds
article: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the article
particle: the opening of Smyth's chapter on particles
conjunction: Smyth's list of the kinds of conjunction
preposition: the opening of Smyth's chapter on prepositions

dual: Smyth on the use of the dual

present: the present proper, the first use Smyth gives
future: the opening of Smyth's section on the future
aorist: the opening of Smyth's section on the aorist indicative
perfect: the opening of Smyth's section on the perfect
pluperfect: the opening of Smyth's section on the pluperfect
future perfect: the opening of Smyth's section on the future perfect

indicative: the opening of Smyth's section on the indicative
subjunctive: Smyth's summary of the uses of the independent subjunctive
optative: the optative of wish, from which the mood takes its name
imperative: the opening of Smyth's section on the imperative
infinitive: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the infinitive
participle: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the participle

active: the opening of Smyth's section on the active voice
middle: the opening of Smyth's section on the middle voice
passive: the opening of Smyth's section on the passive voice
middle or passive: the passive, whose note a. explains that outside the future and aorist the same forms serve as middle and passive

nominative: Smyth on the nominative as the case of the subject
genitive: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the genitive
dative: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the dative
accusative: the opening of Smyth's chapter on the accusative

comparative: Smyth on the use of the comparative
superlative: Smyth on the use of the superlative
